name: EK Baumer
classification_notes: A neo-grotesque system sans classified here under its Uniwidth cut, which gives text and structured information an even rhythm; the wider Baumer system also covers a tighter Headline cut and a Mono companion.
summary: A contemporary sans-serif system in four weights, its Uniwidth cut built for an even rhythm across text and structured information.
description: EK Baumer is structured as a three-part system: a tight Headline cut for expressive large-scale use, this even-spaced Uniwidth cut for text and data, and a Mono cut for technical work. Each part carries four weights with matching italics, stylistic alternates, biform characters and optical size mapping across the family.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes EK Baumer as a disciplined yet versatile typeface system supporting clear hierarchy, controlled variation and contemporary visual communication, with Uniwidth giving a more even rhythm for text and structured information.

name: EK Baumer Mono
classification_notes: The fixed-width cut of the Baumer system, built for coding, tabular data and other operational typography rather than general text.
summary: The monospaced cut of the EK Baumer system, built for coding, tabular data and other technical typography.
description: Baumer Mono shares the system's visual foundation with the Headline and Uniwidth cuts, adapted to a fixed pitch for technical and functional environments. Four weights ship with matching italics, stylistic alternates and circled figures.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes Baumer Mono as extending the system into technical and functional environments, supporting coding structures, tabular data and operational typography.

name: EK Modena
classification_notes: A wide variable superfamily built around fitting an oval shape into a square frame; classified as sans-serif for its proportional cut, with six widths giving it a strong condensed range.
summary: A variable superellipse-inspired superfamily spanning eight weights and six widths, from compressed headlines to sturdy text setting.
description: EK Modena takes the geometry of a superellipse, an oval fitted into a square frame, as its starting shape, then stretches that logic across six widths and eight weights with selected italics. A Mono companion adapts the same design language to a fixed pitch.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes EK Modena as a variable superfamily inspired by the shape of a superellipse, ranging from compressed headline styles to proper widths for long copy with a wide, colourful design space.

name: EK Modena Mono
classification_notes: The monospaced cut of the Modena superfamily, carrying the same superellipse-derived geometry into a fixed-pitch setting.
summary: The fixed-pitch cut of the EK Modena superfamily, keeping its superellipse geometry at a consistent character width.
description: Modena Mono inherits the parent superfamily's eight-weight range and superellipse-derived curves, adapted to monospace for code and tabular use where the proportional cuts wouldn't fit.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet positions Modena Mono within the EK Modena superfamily, inspired by the shape of a superellipse fitted into a square frame.

name: EK Notice Sans
classification_notes: Inspired by fifteenth-century Florentine sans-serif lettering, classified as sans-serif for its stroke construction despite the historical serif-era reference.
summary: The plainest of the three Notice styles, drawing on fifteenth-century Florentine sans-serif lettering with a five-weight range.
description: EK Notice Sans is the restrained member of the Notice trio, sharing its Florentine reference and five-weight range with Notice Classic and Notice Decor but keeping contrast and detailing to a minimum. Vietnamese support extends its reach beyond standard Latin Extended.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes EK Notice as inspired by the Florentine sans-serif style of the fifteenth century combined with an exploration of contrast, with OpenType features letting alternate characters shift between upright and italic forms.

name: EK Notice Classic
classification_notes: The mid-contrast member of the Notice trio, still classified sans-serif but carrying more calligraphic width variation than Notice Sans.
summary: The middle style in the Notice trio, adding calligraphic contrast in stroke width to the family's Florentine-influenced structure.
description: Notice Classic sits between the plain Sans cut and the heavier Decor style, carrying more width variation in its strokes while keeping the five-weight range and Vietnamese-inclusive Latin support common to the trio.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes the Notice family as inspired by the Florentine sans-serif style of the fifteenth century, with varying contrast in character width and stroke thickness across its three styles.

name: EK Notice Decor
classification_notes: The most decorative member of the Notice trio, pushed far enough in contrast and detailing to read as a display face rather than a working text sans.
summary: The most decorative cut in the Notice trio, taking the family's Florentine reference into display territory.
description: Notice Decor pushes the trio's shared Florentine-influenced structure furthest into contrast and ornament, best suited to headline and display use rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet presents Notice Decor as the most expressive of the three Notice styles, sharing the family's Florentine reference and OpenType-driven alternation between upright and italic forms.

name: EK Roumald
classification_notes: A display serif in the Scotch Roman and Century Extended tradition, drawn using a CNC router as a virtual pantograph, which is classified as display given its stated headline use rather than text setting.
summary: A display serif drawing on Scotch Roman and Century Extended, its rounded counters traced from ink slurs in old metal type rather than a clean historical revival.
description: Roumald sits in the tradition of early and late nineteenth-century American display serifs from Linn Boyd Benton and Morris Fuller Benton, but a CNC router stood in for the Benton pantograph during development, and its softened counters borrow from the ink slurs common to small metal type. A Mono companion carries the same references into a fixed pitch.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes Roumald as a display face in the tradition of Scotch and its relative Century Extended, its mechanical reference lending the design a slightly technical look while freeing it from its ancestors' expression.

name: EK Roumald Mono
classification_notes: The fixed-pitch cut of Roumald, carrying its nineteenth-century display serif references into a monospaced setting.
summary: The monospaced companion to Roumald, keeping its neo-classical display serif character at a fixed character width.
description: Roumald Mono shares its parent's Benton-era reference points and CNC-router-drawn counters, adapted to a consistent pitch for tabular or technical use where the proportional cut wouldn't fit.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet positions Roumald Mono alongside Roumald as a display face in the tradition of Scotch and Century Extended, with the same mechanically-derived, rounded counter forms.

name: EK Ultimo
classification_notes: A serif-less reinterpretation of an Antiqua structure, classified as display given its stated genre-blending, playful intent rather than any text-setting role.
summary: An experimental display face blending a futuristic feel with classic Antiqua structure, reworked from Minoru Morita's Rain Drops.
description: EK Ultimo takes its raindrop-like curves and strong contrast from a contemporary reinterpretation of Minoru Morita's Rain Drops, stripping away serifs from the Antiqua structure to land somewhere between genres. It ships in three weights, Regular through Black.
foundry_blurb: Erkin Karamemet describes EK Ultimo as blending a futuristic vibe with classic Antiqua traditions, inspired by its raindrop-like appearance and offering a playful, genre-blending choice for dynamic, expressive projects.
